facts.text: Moose Wilson Road is a fifteen-mile scenic byway connecting the communities of Wilson and Moose in Wyoming's Jackson Hole valley.
Indigenous peoples have utilized the area around Moose Wilson Road for millennia, with archaeological evidence dating back at least eleven thousand years.
Moose Wilson Road winds through diverse habitats, offering sightings of moose, black and grizzly bears, beavers, and herons.
The landscape of Moose Wilson Road features glacial terraces, outwash plains, and steep U-shaped canyons like Death Canyon and Granite Canyon.
Vehicle restrictions prohibit trailers and recreational vehicles exceeding twenty-three feet in length to preserve the integrity of Moose Wilson Road.
Moose Wilson Road typically closes to vehicles from November to mid-May due to heavy snow and winter weather conditions.
